text.p: Gloom surrounding Swedish forestry deepened on Tuesday when AssiDoman, one of the big four groups in the sector and the largest woodland owner by area, reported a 52 percent fall in nine-month profits.

Though AssiDoman's 1.62 billion Swedish crown ($245 million) profit after financial items was exactly in line with the average analyst forecast, the figure was boosted by a windfall property-sale gain of 589 million crowns.
AssiDoman blamed weaker prices across the full range of its forestry products and adverse currency movements.
"The lower prices explain for the most part the deterioration of the result," AssiDoman said in a statement, adding that the stronger crown had also had a negative effect.

A smaller forestry company, Munksjo AB, confirmed the downturn in one of Sweden's core industrial sectors when it announced a pre-tax profit of only 140 million crowns compared with 448 million at the same time last year.
Munksjo also attributed the lower profit to the collapse in pulp prices.
Swedish forestry giants Stora and SCA have already published substantially lower results for the first nine months 1996, and MoDo is due to unveil nine-month figures on Wednesday.

AssiDoman, privatised in 1994 and now one of the most widely held Swedish shares, said weaker prices had hit all its activities ranging from forestry management through timber and pulp to the manufacture of fine paper.
The strengthening of the Swedish crown was calculated to have wreaked 400 million crowns worth of damage to the nine-month result.
"It is a bit disappointing," one London-based analyst said. "If you take away that exceptional item worth nearly 600 million crowns, the figure is weaker than some people were expecting."

Another analyst, Hubert de Marliare of Paribas, said he believed there was a short-term risk that pulp prices could slip still further, adding that it was traditionally hard for forestry companies to curtail production in winter months.
De Marliare said he had downgraded by 27 percent his 1997 average earnings per share forecast for Scandinavian paper companies.
AssiDoman reported a drop in its earnings per share for the nine months to 10.15 crowns versus 21.30 crowns a year ago.
However AssiDoman shares did not suffer from the result, trading three crowns higher at 165 crowns at 1445 GMT.
